gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: The flight was delayed ___ thick fog.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of' + noun phrase gives the cause; although/despite express contrast.

gaps.sentence: ___ keep the audience engaged, the lecturer used live demonstrations.
gaps.explanation: Fronted 'In order to + infinitive' states the purpose of the action.

gaps.sentence: He works as a waiter ___ studying for his degree.
gaps.explanation: 'While' joins two ongoing actions; 'during' takes a noun.

gaps.sentence: The scheme creates hundreds of jobs. ___, it attracts tourism to the region.
gaps.explanation: 'In addition' introduces another benefit of the scheme.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets cost more, but they sold out in minutes.
gaps.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', auxiliary inversion applies: Not only did the tickets cost more.

gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that the evidence was thin, the jury convicted him.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that + clause' converts a clause into the noun phrase that despite requires.
'Firstly' opens a sequence of instructions; eventually/finally close one.
